title: 出塞
author: Wang Changling

translation: The same moon as in Qin times, the same passes as in Han
Ten thousand miles of campaign, and the men have not returned
If only the Flying General of Dragon City were here
No barbarian horse would dare cross the Yin Mountains

annotations.秦时明月汉时关: interlocked phrasing — 'the moon of Qin, the passes of Han' together mean 'timeless frontier'
annotations.飞将: the Flying General — Li Guang, a Han dynasty hero the nomads feared
annotations.教: here read jiào — to let, to allow
annotations.胡马: horses of the northern nomads — shorthand for invading forces
annotations.阴山: the Yin Mountains, a natural defensive line in today's Inner Mongolia

appreciation: Often called the greatest frontier quatrain of the Tang. The first line collapses a thousand years into one image: the moon that saw Qin soldiers still watches Han passes, and still watches us. The lament is quiet — dynasties change, the war never ends — before flaring into a wish for a legendary general who could end it.
